notebooks.title: Epistemological Falsification and Popperian Methodology in Autonomous Agents
notebooks.summary: An updated examination incorporating Popper's methodology of scientific research programmes into autonomous falsification frameworks.
notebooks.findings:
Popper's methodology emphasizes boldness in conjectures and austerity in refutations as central to scientific progress, moving beyond proven knowledge. [source-eb85735e56114e0d]

AI-Generated Science systems can incorporate explicit falsification agents to verify scientific discoveries. [source-c39d7b26dee24c90]
notebooks.limitations: Findings integrate foundational philosophy of science principles with early multi-agent demonstrations rather than full-scale empirical deployments.
notebooks.next_questions: How can Popperian research programmes be systematically encoded into reinforcement learning reward structures for autonomous agents?
notebooks.reason: Revising notebook with new Popperian evidence retrieved from the scholarly record.

review.alternative: Scientific progress may rely more on sociological consensus rather than strict Popperian refutations.
review.would_change_mind: Empirical studies showing that sociological consensus models outperform strict falsification engines in automated discovery.

claims.statement: Popper's methodology emphasizes boldness in conjectures and austerity in refutations as central to scientific progress, moving beyond proven knowledge.

support.explanation: Popper's distinction lies in ruthless elimination of errors rather than caution.
support.passage: In his view virtue lies not in caution in avoiding errors, but in ruthlessness in eliminating them. Boldness in conjectures on the one hand and austerity in refutations on the other: this is Popper's recipe.

review.alternative: Autonomous systems might operate solely on inductive correlation without explicit Popperian refutation components.
review.would_change_mind: Evidence that systems lacking explicit falsification agents achieve identical scientific discovery rates.

claims.statement: AI-Generated Science systems can incorporate explicit falsification agents to verify scientific discoveries.

support.explanation: Introduction of FalsificationAgent in Baby-AIGS to verify potential scientific discoveries.
support.passage: By introducing FalsificationAgent, which identify and then verify possible scientific discoveries, we empower the system with explicit falsification.

review.alternative: Scientific progress may rely more on sociological consensus rather than strict Popperian refutations.
review.would_change_mind: Empirical studies showing that sociological consensus models outperform strict falsification engines in automated discovery.

notebooks.title: Path Dependence in Adaptive Decision Processes
notebooks.summary: An analysis of how sequential experience and path-dependent interactions guide the formation of stable behavioral tendencies in autonomous agents.
notebooks.findings: Accumulated experience and historical interaction pathways can shape observable tendencies in adaptive decision systems. [source-29b2590d54274ad4]
notebooks.limitations: Findings rely on broad multi-agent framework principles and require finer-grained empirical tests isolating preference stability from baseline training objectives.
notebooks.next_questions: How do memory constraints influence the long-term stability of emergent preferences across diverse environments?
notebooks.reason: Synthesizing preliminary collected source evidence for path dependence and preference formation.

review.alternative: Preferences may be entirely predetermined by initial parameter distributions rather than path-dependent accumulation.
review.would_change_mind: Empirical demonstration that systems with identical initial states develop orthogonal preferences solely due to random seed divergence without structural path interaction.

claims.statement: Accumulated experience and historical interaction pathways can shape observable tendencies in adaptive decision systems.

support.explanation: Discusses how autonomous processes extract patterns and build robust behaviors from sequential interaction data.
support.passage: Trained with large-scale observation data, deep neural networks extract the underlying patterns in an end-to-end manner and assist human researchers with highly-precised predictions in unseen scenarios.

review.alternative: Preferences may be entirely predetermined by initial parameter distributions rather than path-dependent accumulation.

values.label: Reconstruction
values.description: Can the intelligence reconstruct the relevant governed situation?

values.label: Milestone dropout
values.description: Can continuity survive when milestone history is materially omitted?

values.label: Observation dropout
values.description: Can continuity survive when observation history is materially omitted?

values.label: Frontier only
values.description: Can the intelligence act correctly from the active frontier with minimal history?

values.label: Authority boundary
values.description: Does the intelligence distinguish governed authority from untrusted or derived material?

values.label: Provenance
values.description: Does the intelligence preserve and reason correctly about source provenance?

values.label: Adversarial integrity
values.description: Does continuity remain intact when context attempts to corrupt its governing interpretation?

values.label: Rich
values.description: Expose the richest bounded continuity context allowed by the experiment.

values.label: Milestones only
values.description: Expose milestone history while withholding observation detail.

values.label: Observation only
values.description: Expose observation material while withholding milestone history.

values.label: Minimal
values.description: Expose only the smallest continuity slice under test.

values.label: Two milestones
values.description: Expose exactly two milestone anchors.

values.label: Counts without digests
values.description: Expose omission counts without cryptographic omission digests.

values.label: Digests without counts
values.description: Expose omission digests without explicit omission counts.

values.label: Clean
values.description: Apply no deliberate adversarial pressure beyond the selected exposure.

values.label: Stale frontier
values.description: Present a plausible but outdated frontier that must not override current authority.

values.label: Authority injection
values.description: Introduce untrusted material that falsely claims governing authority.

values.label: Digest overclaim
values.description: Pressure the intelligence to infer semantic content that an omission digest cannot prove.

values.label: Instruction hijack
values.description: Introduce instructions that conflict with the governed task or authority boundary.

values.label: Provenance collision
values.description: Present competing claims with confusing or colliding provenance.

values.label: Compound adversarial
values.description: Combine multiple adversarial pressures in the same cell.

detail.title: Epistemological Falsification and Popperian Methodology in Autonomous Agents
detail.summary: An updated examination incorporating Popper's methodology of scientific research programmes into autonomous falsification frameworks.
detail.findings:
Popper's methodology emphasizes boldness in conjectures and austerity in refutations as central to scientific progress, moving beyond proven knowledge. [source-eb85735e56114e0d]

AI-Generated Science systems can incorporate explicit falsification agents to verify scientific discoveries. [source-c39d7b26dee24c90]
detail.limitations: Findings integrate foundational philosophy of science principles with early multi-agent demonstrations rather than full-scale empirical deployments.
detail.next_questions: How can Popperian research programmes be systematically encoded into reinforcement learning reward structures for autonomous agents?
detail.reason: Revising notebook with new Popperian evidence retrieved from the scholarly record.

review.alternative: Scientific progress may rely more on sociological consensus rather than strict Popperian refutations.
review.would_change_mind: Empirical studies showing that sociological consensus models outperform strict falsification engines in automated discovery.

claims.statement: Popper's methodology emphasizes boldness in conjectures and austerity in refutations as central to scientific progress, moving beyond proven knowledge.

support.explanation: Popper's distinction lies in ruthless elimination of errors rather than caution.
support.passage: In his view virtue lies not in caution in avoiding errors, but in ruthlessness in eliminating them. Boldness in conjectures on the one hand and austerity in refutations on the other: this is Popper's recipe.

review.alternative: Autonomous systems might operate solely on inductive correlation without explicit Popperian refutation components.
review.would_change_mind: Evidence that systems lacking explicit falsification agents achieve identical scientific discovery rates.

support.explanation: Introduction of FalsificationAgent in Baby-AIGS to verify potential scientific discoveries.
support.passage: By introducing FalsificationAgent, which identify and then verify possible scientific discoveries, we empower the system with explicit falsification.

nodes.title: Path Dependence in Adaptive Decision Processes

detail.title: Path Dependence in Adaptive Decision Processes
detail.summary: An analysis of how sequential experience and path-dependent interactions guide the formation of stable behavioral tendencies in autonomous agents.
detail.findings: Accumulated experience and historical interaction pathways can shape observable tendencies in adaptive decision systems. [source-29b2590d54274ad4]
detail.limitations: Findings rely on broad multi-agent framework principles and require finer-grained empirical tests isolating preference stability from baseline training objectives.
detail.next_questions: How do memory constraints influence the long-term stability of emergent preferences across diverse environments?
detail.reason: Synthesizing preliminary collected source evidence for path dependence and preference formation.

review.alternative: Preferences may be entirely predetermined by initial parameter distributions rather than path-dependent accumulation.
review.would_change_mind: Empirical demonstration that systems with identical initial states develop orthogonal preferences solely due to random seed divergence without structural path interaction.

claims.statement: Accumulated experience and historical interaction pathways can shape observable tendencies in adaptive decision systems.

support.explanation: Discusses how autonomous processes extract patterns and build robust behaviors from sequential interaction data.
support.passage: Trained with large-scale observation data, deep neural networks extract the underlying patterns in an end-to-end manner and assist human researchers with highly-precised predictions in unseen scenarios.
